traveller:
A traveller is a visitor who seeks deeper connection & understanding, even cultural immersion & authentic experiences of the places & people they are visiting.

This usually requires lingering, genuine curiosity, listening, asking good question & developing empathy for the experiences & outlooks of others … habits which hitchhiking often fosters! Unhurried conversations with locals, an effort to remember unusual names, important words and new customs, a willingness to go off the beaten track & a cheerful acceptance of both surprises & long 'pauses' are all part of the package.

These habits of heart & mind will be important for those who want to explore & contemplate what was revealed to John — & all who read it — in the Apocalypse.
tourist:
Tourists visit destinations primarily for short-term recreation & 'sightseeing', often relying on comfort zones & packaged itineraries. They often say they have 'done Turkey' after a week os rushing through a fast-paced checklist of desirable highlights — & photographing them, of course! This kind of visitor can be impatient to get on to the next highlight long before they have gained any insight into a place, the stories it holds or everyday realities faced by the people there.

A 'tourist' in the Apocalypse will probably find this guide less helpful than a 'traveller'. There won't be quick answers to the popular questions or a 'cheatsheet' to break the 'code'. You will have to 'chew your own food' (as the old rabbis used to tell their students), to linger rather than rush over passages & digest their meanings for the original readers first, & then for us now.

Insights provided by the guide for each passage will hopefully help this process along & I expect many of your questions will gradually be answered. The most important process, though, will be listening long enough to hear - & begin answering - the questions the Apocalypse is asking us.
